Interestingly enough, when asked for a list of devices affected by the change, a Microsoft representative began listing Droid phones./s

I just upgraded my Lumia 930. It's got it's pros and cons, but I would say the major improvement is to the Outlook mail client. Now I actually feel like I can use my phone to send e-mails, rather than feeling "oh bugger I have to reply to this on my phone". My impression so far:

Pros

  • Very much improved responsiveness - quicker and easier to use
  • More detailed control over which apps can get access to what (this was a major issue before as you either allowed the app access to everything it wanted, or you couldn't install it)
  • Detailed privacy settings (you can control what information which app sends)
  • Much needed improvement of Outlook mail client. - Easier to switch between mail boxes, ability to from the same client reply from differenty mail boxes without going to them individually, ability to decide what swipe left/right does (quick actions, like I swipe the mail right and it becomes read/unread, swiping left opens move to folder. Actions to choose are read/unread, delete, move to folder, and set/unset flag).

Cons

  • For some reason, some of the apps are no longer able to rotate the screen, so you're stuck with the vertical view - which is absolutely horrible for typing
  • Shittier music app - this is the third time they completely fuck up the music app. The first time I used a Windows Phone in 2012 they didn't have playlists (like wtf, is this the 80s? Even Winamp had this in the 90s, it's not like it's difficult). Then they introduced it, but you couldn't create them anywhere but your phone (the PC app didn't allow for creation of playlists), and there was no good way to edit them. Now that Nokia is out of the picture they completely scrap the old app and use a new one... which removed the possibilty of adding several songs to a playlist! So now you have to individually select one song at a time, chose "add to playlist" then select the playlist. Like, WHAT, the fuck is the problem with doing a decent music player?
  • Some apps close down randomly - well, it's not really closing, it's more of opening the start screen, I'm guessing bug here.

Overall I'd say that it's an improvement. I get the feeling that they've moved away from the consumer side and focused on the enterprise aspect (integration with Office etc.) which is nice since I use mine for work. The apps not rotating to horizontal is only for one app so far, and it actually made a previous app that was stuck in vertical be able to switch to horizontal so I'm kinda "meh" on that one. What they do need to fix though is their music player. For fuck sake, it's 2016, that shit shouldn't be hard. If you're going to remove a previously working client, make sure you have one that is at least on par with the one you're deleting.
